headline: Google has put Anthropic's newest Claude models inside its own Antigravity coding tool, but only for paying subscribers.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: a real product change confirmed in Google's documentation, but unannounced, single outlet, and limited to paid tiers.
importance_line: Developers on Google's paid AI plans can now pick Claude Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 against Gemini in the same tool and on one Google bill, which matters to teams choosing where their coding budget goes and to Anthropic's reach, though Google has said nothing about the change and the pricing details come from a third party.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that Google's model documentation for Antigravity, the agentic coding environment Google built after its roughly $2.4 billion Windsurf licensing and hiring deal, now lists Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5, available only to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and not on trial, free, AI Plus or Enterprise plans. The tool had been running the older Claude 4.6 models for more than a week after Anthropic shipped the 5.5 versions in late September, and Google has not mentioned the addition in a blog post or changelog.
notes: Exact date of the change not stated; the article was published 3 Oct 2026. Pricing figures attributed by the outlet to CloudZero.
